regions.name: Western Pacific warm pool
regions.why: The tropical atmosphere above the warmest ocean on Earth, from the surface to the tropopause.

regions.name: Central Amazon
regions.why: The largest rain forest: are its dry seasons getting hotter and drier?

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

TQV.label: Water vapour in the air column
TQV.simple: All the water vapour above a spot, from the ground to the top of the atmosphere — the millimetres of water you would get if it all rained out at once.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

story.text: Air temperature — Western Pacific warm pool: +0.21 °C per decade (95 % range +0.176 to +0.241). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 4e-16, t-test p = 4.1e-12. Eva: Since 2011, 80 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Air temperature — Central Amazon: +0.37 °C per decade (95 % range +0.287 to +0.451). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 5.2e-13, t-test p = 3e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 77 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Precipitation — Central Amazon: -0.50 mm/day per decade (95 % range -0.646 to -0.329). Significant falling trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.8e-07, t-test p = 4.7e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 81 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Model note: both series come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, not from two independent instruments: confirm it with an independent dataset before calling it a finding.
